title: Integrate the PostgreSQL capture runtime and feedback loop
description:
Objective / why
Own the missing end-to-end `boring-cdc run` path from CopyBoth receive through bounded spool, atomic SQLite publication/source-state commit, and safe PostgreSQL feedback.

Exact scope

Authoritative contract

design:
The runtime acquires both SQLite and deterministic source advisory locks. It parses CopyBoth frames and Origin metadata, spools a bounded whole transaction, atomically commits complete events plus durable source boundary, then sends a standby-status packet whose write/flush/apply positions are all that persisted boundary. It immediately answers requested keepalives without copying `wal_end`. Reconnect and shutdown always reconcile from durable state.

## Creation-floor hardening
Store the server-established slot-creation consistent point separately from nullable durable transaction-end progress. Never fabricate a source transaction or proactively acknowledge the floor. Before importer acknowledgements, requested replies may only use the pinned zero sentinel or verified floor; later WAL is not feedback-eligible.

## Ownership and command-endpoint hardening
`run` owns a bounded Unix-domain mutating command endpoint and persists idempotent request/result records; status TCP remains read-only. Requests bind ID, run/epoch/config/table-set/anchor/generation fingerprints, dry-run digest/expiry, and peer identity. Offline mutations acquire both locks and reconcile. The source advisory lock uses a dedicated non-pooled backend PID/nonce plus monotonic ownership deadline; uncertain loss fences all dispatch and exits without in-place reacquire, and successors wait then reconcile.

## Bounded fixed control rows
Both published control relations contain exactly one administration-seeded immutable-key row. The runtime credential has column-limited UPDATE only; no INSERT, DELETE, or key change. Heartbeat/fence updates require exactly one affected row, and each fence uses a unique nonce while SQLite retains history.

## Creation-floor hardening acceptance
Fixtures cover PostgreSQL variants exposing null or the creation floor in confirmed state, crash/restart before the first transaction, requested replies, importer-gated later feedback, and prove the floor never populates durable transaction progress.
